alex: Ran an eviction-threshold + streaming KV handoff bench across A100 / H100 / L40S. TL;DR: H100 ~1.2x A100 on default L40S profiles; L40S unstable at bsz48 for seq >= 2048 and we saw a kernel selector flip to fused_paged at seq=4096 that caused a p99 spike. Posting quick numbers and repro steps.

priya: which stack? driver / torch / runtime?

alex: cuda 12.1, nvidia driver 535.54, torch 2.2.0, triton 2.1.0, runtime branch: serve/main@c3f9b. Kernels built with -O3, cublas v12.1. Bench command I used:

alex: ```
./bench_attn --model=redwood-medium --kernels=flash,paged,fused_paged --gpus=A100,H100,L40S --seqs=512,1024,2048,4096 --bsz=48 --kv-policy=streaming_prefetch --warmup=200 --iters=500
```

mikhail: can you paste the core outputs for bsz48? need throughput + p99 + gpu-mem

alex: here's compact output (bsz48):

alex: ```
H100  seq512  thr=8600 tok/s  p99=12ms  gpu_mem=28.1GB  kernel=flash_fused
H100  seq1024 thr=6100 tok/s  p99=18ms  gpu_mem=31.3GB  kernel=flash_fused
H100  seq2048 thr=4200 tok/s  p99=32ms  gpu_mem=34.9GB  kernel=flash_fused
H100  seq4096 thr=2100 tok/s  p99=120ms gpu_mem=36.6GB  kernel=fused_paged   <-- p99 jump

A100  seq512  thr=7200 tok/s  p99=14ms  gpu_mem=29.0GB  kernel=flash
A100  seq1024 thr=5020 tok/s  p99=20ms  gpu_mem=33.0GB  kernel=flash
A100  seq2048 thr=3500 tok/s  p99=38ms  gpu_mem=35.8GB  kernel=flash
A100  seq4096 thr=1800 tok/s  p99=140ms gpu_mem=37.2GB  kernel=fused_paged

L40S  seq512  thr=5200 tok/s  p99=20ms  gpu_mem=23.0GB  kernel=flash
L40S  seq1024 thr=3600 tok/s  p99=36ms  gpu_mem=26.4GB  kernel=flash
L40S  seq2048 thr=1600 tok/s  p99=210ms gpu_mem=30.1GB  kernel=kernel_fallback  <-- instability
L40S  seq4096 thr=700 tok/s  p99=430ms  gpu_mem=31.0GB  kernel=fused_paged  <-- bad
```

jamie: that L40S seq2048 p99=210ms is worrying. The kernel name 'kernel_fallback' indicates selector dropped to CPU or slow path? Did you capture profiler trace?

alex: grabbed a short nsight trace for the seq2048 failure. nvprof shows a lot of small memcpy kernels and SM efficiency dropped to 22% around the spike. Also saw frequent kv cache evictions causing reupload churn.

mikhail: possible causes: 1) eviction threshold too aggressive causing KV spill thrash, 2) kernel candidate ordering in selector picks fused_paged for long seq and falls back on fragments, 3) alignment/tiling mismatch on L40S for our build. Try forcing kernel order to prefer flash over fused_paged.

sara: current kv prefetch threshold is 0.7 for streaming_prefetch. i've seen better stability at 0.5 on L40S for bsz>=32. lowering threshold reduces reuploads but may increase memory usage.

alex: snippet to force kernel preference in runtime config:

alex: ```json
{"kernel_selector":{"priorities":["flash_fused","flash","paged"],"eviction_threshold":0.5}}
```

alex: plan: 1) mikhail, can you run H100 + forced kernel order for seq4096 bsz48 and confirm if p99 stays low? 2) i'll run L40S with eviction_threshold=0.5 and repeat seq sweep. 3) if stable, we add a runtime guard to prefer flash for heavy-bsz streaming until we have tiled-paged fixes.

mikhail: will run H100 now, queueing job on perf-cluster. perf-bot: job queued for run 3345680012 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

perf-bot: perf job 3345680012 started on h100-02, ETA ~25m

jamie: if H100 stays stable with forced order, we should change selector to prefer flash for bsz>=32 + seq>=1024 as a short-term fallback.

sara: agree. also add a regression test that sweeps eviction_thresholds 0.4..0.8 on L40S in CI so we catch thrash early.

alex: thanks all. i'll post follow-up when runs finish. attaching nsight capture link in thread when available. :eyes:
